C-SITE-COUNTERS.Name: First-party counters: governed settings, an honest CSP allowance and tests for the collector tag
C-SITE-COUNTERS.ApprovalBasis: Owner instruction in chat on 2026-10-27 («го») accepting the refresh finding F1/F2 for branch c/analytics-landing: the counters shipped without a change bundle, and the built CSP omits the collector origin so the shipped pages cannot report anything.
C-SITE-COUNTERS.Summary: The landing and docs pages load a first-party counter (site/public/analytics.js) whose key arrives from PUBLIC_COLLECT_KEY and whose endpoint defaults to the project's own collector. The refresh audit of 2026-10-27 found the feature inert (the meta CSP did not admit the collector origin, so every beacon was blocked) and ungoverned (no settings entry, no test, no verification scenario, and the docs head emitted the tag even without a key while the landing did not). Within minutes the owner landed the blunt half of the fix — a hardcoded dash origin in connect-src (commit 128636f8) — which restored delivery but left the tag inconsistent, the allowance detached from the configured endpoint, and nothing pinned. This change completes it: the collector resolves through resolveSiteSettings like every other provider, the tag exists only when configured and is identical on both surfaces, connect-src derives its allowance from that same endpoint (so a custom endpoint moves both and a keyless build advertises neither), tests/site pins all of it, and M-053/V-M-053 record the behaviour.

Problem.Description: The counter bypassed the settings layer, differed between docs and landing, and had no test or verification entry; its CSP allowance was hardcoded to one host instead of following the configured endpoint, so any other endpoint would have been blocked silently and a keyless build still advertised the owner's collector.
Problem.RootCauseTimestamp: 2026-10-27 refresh audit of branch c/analytics-landing (built dist CSP inspected).

Goals.R-1: resolveSiteSettings(env) returns collect: { key, endpoint } when PUBLIC_COLLECT_KEY is set and null otherwise; the key shape is validated before it is inlined and a malformed key fails the build with the existing BLOCK_RESOLVE_ANALYTICS marker.
Goals.R-2: One description of the collector tag (src + data-key + data-endpoint + defer, base-aware) is used by both surfaces; docs and landing emit it exactly when configured and emit nothing otherwise.
Goals.R-3: cspFor/applyCsp admit the collector origin in connect-src exactly when the collector is configured, derived from the same endpoint the tag carries (superseding commit 128636f8's hardcoded dash entry); no other directive widens, and an unconfigured build carries no collector origin at all.
Goals.R-4: tests/site/analytics.test.mjs pins resolution (default endpoint, custom endpoint, malformed key), tag emission with and without a key on both surfaces, the connect-src allowance, and the runtime contract of analytics.js: no request without a key, one beacon to the configured endpoint with the key as a query parameter when a batch flushes.
Goals.R-5: M-053 lists the site sources it actually owns and V-M-053 gains the scenario and the command that prove the collector contract.

C-SITE-COUNTERS.Dependencies: site/scripts/csp.mjs and site/.vitepress/landing.mjs are consumed by config.mts and check-dist.mjs; both keep their existing call shapes (opts carry one more optional field).

Constraints.Constraint: No third-party provider behaviour changes: GA4, Cloudflare and Umami host toggles stay exactly as they are.

The collector stays first-party and cookieless; the key is public by design and bound to the host by the collector's Origin check — this change does not add a secret to the client beyond the key the owner already injects.
An unconfigured build must remain identical: no collector tag, no new connect-src entry.
No new npm dependency; the site build keeps its single-command contract.

NonGoals.NonGoal: The collector service itself (dash host), its storage, or its Origin policy — only the client wiring and its CSP allowance are in scope.
Removing GA4 or the comparison-week setup.
A consent gate for the first-party counters beyond what site/public/consent.js already does for GA4 (the counters carry no cookies and no cross-site identifiers).
Reworking site/scripts/check-dist.mjs into a CSP/analytics cross-check; the unit suite pins the contract.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A build with PUBLIC_COLLECT_KEY set emits the collector tag on the landing and on docs pages and a CSP whose connect-src contains the collector origin; the same build without the key emits neither the tag nor the origin.
resolveSiteSettings rejects a malformed key with BLOCK_RESOLVE_ANALYTICS, defaults the endpoint, and accepts an explicit PUBLIC_COLLECT_ENDPOINT.
tests/site/analytics.test.mjs passes in the standard matrix and covers the four R-4 cases, including the analytics.js beacon URL and its no-key early return on fake browser globals.
M-053 Paths and V-M-053 scenario-15 name the collector; the existing `npx vitest run tests/site` command already runs the new suite; grace lint --assertions current stays at its recorded baseline.

C-SITE-COUNTERS.VerificationIntent: npx vitest run tests/site/analytics.test.mjs; npx vitest run tests/site; cd site && PUBLIC_COLLECT_KEY=demo-key npm run build, then inspect connect-src and the tag in .vitepress/dist; grace lint --path . --change C-SITE-COUNTERS --assertions final --run-commands.

Approval.ApprovedBy: owner (chat, 2026-10-27): «го» after the refresh report (findings F1/F2)
Approval.ApprovalScope: Implementation, tests and governance deltas on branch c/analytics-landing; no version bump, no tag, no publication.
